scope: Actual documentary comparison of the fixed new passage frame, controls and source-qualified material observations. Categories are judgments about components, not probabilities or mutually exclusive ownership of entire texts.
shared_rule: R1 requires a specific operation/role match and dated carrier to identify a local contribution. A language-contact claim does not identify that carrier. R5 endpoint organization is recorded separately from a demonstrated rewrite of an earlier surviving passage.

R1.bearing: Local workers could contribute practical content, but no particular post-Harappan work/teacher chain is traced.

R2.bearing: The independently attributed inherited poet/patron role and Soma/Haoma frame supply specific external repertoire explanations; the Greek role cluster is comparative support, not a proof for every occupation.

R3.bearing: Clients and specialists could meet through wider exchange; this text gives no discriminating route.

R4.bearing: Workers seeking relevant clients and household task diversity can arise under recurring practical/economic conditions.

R5.bearing: Occupational examples are visibly organized under a Soma refrain; their historical first organization or earlier reworking is unobserved.

comparisons.endpoint_observed: Poetic occupational/resource portrayal, including different household tasks.
comparisons.decision: The repertoire is attested; a uniquely required local origin is unsupported. No bead production operation is specified.

comparisons.component: Practical imagery, peer competence and differentiated ritual performance

R1.bearing: Local practical routines could supply images or knowledge; the processor-to-poet carrier and specific donor are unobserved.

R2.bearing: Comparative scholarship supports inherited poetic roles/formulae; Old Avestan addressed speech and ritual specialists prevent broad verbal sophistication from being uniquely local.

R3.bearing: Contact can introduce practical images or learning relationships, but no route is identified.

R4.bearing: Sifting/fashioning/measuring can be independently useful models for evaluating speech and coordinating work.

R5.bearing: Practical-to-conceptual analogy and peer/role organization are directly visible at this poem's stage; a specific earlier passage's reorganization is not observed.

comparisons.endpoint_observed: Meal-sifting analogy and depicted peer evaluation, affiliation, assembly recognition and ritual role/action distinctions.
comparisons.exploratory_refinement: Recipient specialists can turn a useful operation into a model for conceptual evaluation. This is proposed within the already fixed complete hymn, after initial reading.
comparisons.decision: A positive practical-to-conceptual relation is directly attested. Formal school/examination and a Harappan donor remain further hypotheses.

R1.bearing: Local plant handling is source-qualified, but current material contexts lack the poem's linked plow/yoke/sow/harvest account and an identified carrier.

R2.bearing: Iranian pastoral/cultivation traditions provide external repertoire, but the selected Old Avestan phrases are not this operation sequence.

R3.bearing: Crop and technical vocabulary can diffuse regionally; bīja's donor remains unresolved.

R4.bearing: Sowing followed by crop maturation/harvest reflects common constraints and is not a rare signature by itself.

R5.bearing: The poem connects equipment/operations to song, divine favor and sacrifice. That organization is directly observed, while an earlier textual source remains untraced.

comparisons.endpoint_observed: Agricultural vocabulary/relations used in a ritual exhortation; crop species and implement geometry unspecified.
comparisons.decision: The new crop/material evidence establishes narrower endpoints. It does not identify the poem's agricultural origin or a full operation-order transmission.

comparisons.component: Well receptacles, straps and stone-wheel imagery

R1.bearing: No selected material record provides the same contextualized fittings and dated local successors.

R2.bearing: The ritual frame has an inherited explanation; the specific equipment origin remains untraced in the bounded Iranian controls.

R3.bearing: Water-moving equipment can travel through exchange; a particular route is not observed.

R4.bearing: Practical lifting constraints can generate receptacles, straps and wheels; exact arrangement and rarity need comparative evidence.

R5.bearing: The same hymn includes Soma and a well sunk without digging. Ritual use of equipment imagery is observed; historical recoding from a known earlier manual is not.

comparisons.endpoint_observed: Several named fittings in poetic context, with a nonliteral cue.
comparisons.decision: A prospective distinctive-parts comparison is possible. The present text does not determine a unique pulley/water machine, irrigation capacity or excavated construction event.

R1.bearing: An attributed non-Indo-Aryan word can be compatible with local contact but supplies neither a named Harappan language nor an operation carrier.

R2.bearing: Inherited and earlier borrowed Indo-Iranian material can coexist. A shared yava comparison is outside this selected frame and cannot identify its crop.

R3.bearing: The inspected scholar allows other regional languages and wider substrates; donor geography remains unresolved for bīja.

R4.bearing: The practical operation can be reconstructed or retained while its name changes; word history need not equal operation history.

R5.bearing: Lexical choice in a received hymn and later sense lists can organize knowledge; the inspected entries do not date each meaning shift.

comparisons.endpoint_observed: Eight prespecified lemma checks plus one explicitly post-selection term; specific glosses and attributed etymological disagreement/uncertainty.
comparisons.decision: The lexical control narrows applicability. Neither the absent lāṅgala nor the absent grain-yava can become a selected-hymn origin marker.

R1.bearing: Some represented arts can retain local practical content, but no Harappan route is traced.

R2.bearing: Inherited ritual/medical/verbal components remain possible; this selected list does not establish each origin.

R3.bearing: A larger repertoire may draw on regional exchange; its specific acquisitions are unrecorded here.

R4.bearing: Prediction, calculation and treatment address recurring problems and could be reconstructed.

R5.bearing: Normative classification and livelihood/food-support rules are directly attested at this text's stage. This supports endpoint organization, not a demonstrated redaction of a particular earlier surviving passage.

comparisons.endpoint_observed: A represented repertoire reclassified by permitted livelihood in a normative prose passage.
comparisons.decision: Later literature can show intellectual organization of varied arts. It cannot backdate the list to Mature Harappan cities or supply an actual occupational census.
